channel.title: Recall

item.author: Sankari Nair
item.description:
Hello everyone! This release is all about bringing your read-it-later URLs to life by getting your content into Recall. You can now import reading lists straight from a CSV, watch exactly what succeeds or needs attention, and jump right to your new cards. We have also released a new flow so you can save your chat outputs to either one new card or any existing card, improved the images for EPUB and social saves, and squashed a wide range of bugs across saving, sync, and mobile.

Import your reading lists from CSV

  • Bring links from Raindrop, Instapaper, or your own spreadsheet into Recall. Choose CSV of URLs under Add Content, Bulk import, or drop a CSV onto your library.
  • Recall reads the URL, title, and tags columns when present, skips duplicate links and cards already in your library, and shows how many links are ready before you begin.
  • Import up to 1,000 links at a time. For larger files, upload the same CSV again to bring in the next batch.
  • Your links can be any form of content that Recall supports: YouTube, podcasts, social posts, etc.
  • Available on Plus and Max. Imports save the original content without automatically creating AI summaries, and Max users can run bulk AI actions afterwards.

Clearer progress for imports and bulk actions

  • CSV, Pocket, browser bookmark, and Markdown imports now share one consistent progress experience with bulk uploads and AI actions.
  • See what is waiting, what is being processed, and how many cards were added, already existed, or failed. Failed imports show a reason when available and move to the top when the batch finishes.
  • Keep browsing your library while a batch runs, then use View cards to open the cards from that batch.
  • Canceling a batch keeps cards already saved and gives you a clearer account of completed and unfinished work.

Save chat answers to the notebook you choose

  • Add an answer to a new notebook card or search for an existing card to keep related ideas together.
  • Recall remembers your choice for the conversation so the next answer goes to the same card, or you can pick a destination each time.
  • Use Undo if you add an answer by mistake.

Share and export your EPUB books

  • The first page of your EPUB now becomes the main image for the Recall card
  • Send an EPUB to Recall directly from the share sheet on iOS or Android.
  • Exporting an EPUB card or your full library now includes the original book file alongside your Markdown notes.

Improvements and Bugs

Improvements

  • File uploads now let you review selected files in a compact list, remove individual files, or add more before starting. The choice between combining images into one card and creating separate cards is clearer.
  • Recall now attempts to restore missing or broken card thumbnails when a working source image is available. Recovery works in grid, list, and table views without changing your cards' dates or library order, and Wikipedia thumbnails look sharper.
  • Returning to your library restores your scroll position, and navigation stays consistent as you move between pages.
  • LinkedIn short links beginning with lnkd.in now resolve to their destination before Recall saves them.
  • Age-restricted social content saves the link and available public details, with a clear warning when the full content cannot be retrieved.

Imports and notebooks

  • A failed link or connection no longer stops the rest of an import from progressing.
  • Markdown imports now show a clearer error for unreadable or corrupt files, and we fixed import failures caused by ordinary text containing parentheses and percent signs.
  • Copying a notebook link's URL now works more reliably across web and mobile.
  • More reliable batch tags keep imported cards together and make them easier to find after an upload or retry.

Sync, tags, and the extension

  • Fixed another cause of initial sync failures when bringing a large library onto a new device.
  • Improved loading reliability by waiting for sign-in to finish before fetching account data.

Mobile and sign-in

  • Fixed a crash on older iPhones and iPads when opening cards or chat containing Markdown.
  • Fixed another iOS 15 reader compatibility issue that prevented reader content from loading.
  • Fixed mobile file sharing failures when shared filenames contain spaces or special characters.

Coming Next

  • RSS feeds to bring content straight into Recall.
  • A smoother mobile experience with less waiting for content to load.
  • MCP 2.0 with write access to Recall.
item.title: Recall Release Notes, September 25, 2026: Import 1000 URLs in CSV, Save chat outputs to one card, and better images for EPUB and social saves

item.author: Sankari Nair
item.description:
Hello everyone. This release opens up new kinds of content for your second brain. You can now read, search, and chat with EPUB books, keep a whole set of photos together as one card, and let Recall read the text hidden inside the images in your social posts. We also made search on mobile faster and simpler. Alongside all of that, there is a long list of fixes across chat, imports, exports, and device sync.

EPUB books

  • Upload an .epub from Add Content or drop it onto your library, and each book becomes a card you can read, search, and chat with. This brings your books into the same place as your articles, videos, and notes.
  • Add one at a time, or upload up to 10 together on Plus and Max. Each file can be up to 20 MB.

Read the images in social posts + Carousel support

  • Save a photo post from X, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, or LinkedIn, and Recall now reads the text inside the images and adds a visual description, so you capture information that lives in a screenshot, infographic, or carousel.
  • Carousel images stay in order, each with its own title and extracted text, and LinkedIn carousel support now picks up slides that were previously missed.
  • Posts with both images and video keep the image content alongside the extracted video content. Video-only posts continue to use their caption and transcript.
  • Please note that the OCR on social posts is only on images and not on videos as yet

Several photos, one card

  • Add a set of images without turning every photo into its own card, which is ideal for handwritten notes, whiteboards, and screenshots that belong together. Select several images in Add Content or drag and drop them, and they become one card by default.
  • Choose Create separate cards for each image if you want to split them. Recall reads the text and describes each image, keeping everything together in the reader so you can search and chat with the result.
  • On iOS and Android you can share one or several photos straight from your phone's share sheet, with the same choice to combine or separate.
  • Multiple-image uploads are on Plus and Max, up to 10 at a time. Bulk AI summaries and tags are on Max and follow your AI action settings.

Mobile search improvements

  • Search now happens directly in your library, so you can find cards, select several results, and run an action without opening a separate search window.
  • Tag and source filters open in bottom sheets with larger controls, and selecting filters no longer keeps bringing up the keyboard.

Improvements and Bugs

Improvements

  • Better chat searches across topics: when chat searches your library in several ways, it now ranks results against each search and keeps room for those different results, so one search is less likely to crowd out the others.
  • Export progress: exporting your knowledge base now shows progress so you can see that a large export is still running.

Chat

  • Chat on iPhone and Safari: fixed a crash triggered by typing in chat that could affect all devices.
  • Chat messages saving: fixed a cause of answers disappearing or failing to save after chat consulted many sources.
  • Chat getting stuck: Recall now retries stalled or empty responses, and a restarted reply cleanly replaces the unfinished part instead of joining a second answer.

Notebooks

  • Android notebook controls: the toolbar and slash commands stay visible with Gboard's floating keyboard.
  • Notebook drag and drop: the block handle stays aligned after scrolling, and listening to a notebook no longer leaves blocks locked against dragging after a reload.
  • Tables from chat: copying a table into a notebook no longer adds extra blank lines inside its cells.

Sync

  • Changes reaching your other devices: fixed a sync timing issue that could miss card, note, or tag changes made while another device was syncing, including deleted tags remaining in suggestions.
  • Large libraries syncing: fixed failures when syncing a library with large notebooks to a new device.

Saving and imports

  • Social saves: failed X and LinkedIn extractions have additional retry and recovery paths.
  • Saving after time away: fixed saves failing because your sign-in session needed refreshing after the app had been in the background.
  • Obsidian and Markdown imports: a note with invalid YAML metadata no longer stops the rest of a vault import.
  • Duplicate summaries: the extension widget no longer inserts a second detailed-summary toggle.

Exports

  • Large exports: fixed failures when exporting large libraries to a zip file by streaming the file to avoid out-of-memory issues.
  • Markdown exports: quotes and special characters in card titles no longer break exported metadata.

Tags

  • Tag navigation: fixed cases where the tag tree appeared blank or the tag picker stopped responding, and long tag names now stay within the filter layout.

Mobile and display

  • Mobile layouts: menus stay inside the screen's safe area, and the sign-in footer stays visible when the logout warning appears.

Coming Next

Three big things are on the way.

  1. RSS feeds, our number one most requested feature, so the blogs, newsletters, and sites you follow land in Recall automatically.
  2. A faster mobile experience, with far less waiting for content to load wherever you are.
  3. MCP 2.0, unlocking write access so your connected tools can add to Recall, not just read from it.

item.author: Sankari Nair
item.description:
This is a packed one!

Safari users, your wait is over. The Recall extension is now live on Safari and Edge, with a smoother experience for everyone, including adding connections right from the browser. If you have not tried it yet, install it on your browser of choice today: https://www.recall.it/download

Another long-awaited one, OCR on images. Photos, screenshots, and scribbles can finally become real cards. Plus faster ways to add content, with 10 URLs at a time or drag and drop into your library.

And a bigger step towards a smarter knowledge base. Chat suggestions now prompt you with questions drawn from what you have saved, and they sharpen as you add more.

What's New

Extension updates

  • The Recall extension is now live on Safari (Mac) and Microsoft Edge, in addition to Chrome and Firefox. Save a page, get an instant summary, and chat with it without leaving the tab.
  • You can now add connections while editing a notebook directly in the browser extension, so you do not need to jump back to the app.
  • To ensure that you are getting the most out of Recall, we spent some time putting together a detailed tutorial so that you are familiar with just how powerful the browser extension is.

Images as cards

Those handwritten notes, those screenshots, all of it can come to life. Below is a handwritten recipe from my grandmother on how to make her special spice blend. Now in Recall alongside all my recipes.

  • Upload a JPEG, PNG, WebP, or HEIC photo and Recall turns it into a searchable card.
  • AI reads any text in the image, describes what is in the picture, and generates a title, summary, and tags.
  • The image becomes the card cover and appears in the reader with the extracted text underneath, so you can search it and chat with it like any other save.
  • Add one image at a time from Add Content or by dropping it onto your library.

Next up, we'll enable you to add bulk images and also process OCR on social posts.

Chat suggestions

Recall now suggests questions, so you do not have to start from a blank chat.

  • On a card, you get questions tailored to that specific save. Click one to start chatting.
  • In your library on desktop, a Suggested questions panel pulls questions from what you have saved and shows which cards they relate to. You can hide the panel anytime, and dismissed questions stay gone.
  • In Chat, new users get starter questions to learn Recall. Once you have a few cards, you will see prompts about themes, connections, contradictions, and gaps across your knowledge. Used questions rotate out for new ones.
  • Suggestions also appear when you chat with a card from the extension.

Bulk URL import

Paste up to 10 links into Add Content (space, comma, or semicolon separated) and create them as cards in one go, with the same progress tracking as bulk PDF uploads.

Drag and drop to add content

On your main library page, you can drop PDFs, images, text files, Markdown files, or a Markdown zip to create a card or start an import.

Unlinked mentions

On a card's Connections tab, Recall now suggests other cards that mention it in their text but are not linked yet. Link them in one click, with a preview of where each mention appears, and undo if you change your mind.

Share from your phone

On iOS and Android, sharing a card, quiz, challenge, or referral now opens the system share sheet, so you can send it to Messages, WhatsApp, or Mail instead of only copying the link.

Improvements and Bugs

  • Exporting a PDF card to Markdown now includes the original PDF in the zip, and PDF cards show a downloadable source chip under the title.
  • Shared Google AI Mode conversations now save correctly as cards.
  • Facebook story links using facebook.com/story.php are now recognized as posts.

Bug fixes

  • Regenerating connections no longer creates multiple copies of the card's main topic or duplicates mention snippets under a connection.
  • Shared Facebook links such as facebook.com/share/... can be saved as cards again.
  • PDFs that previously showed a blank white screen on some older iOS devices now open normally.
  • The PDF annotation layer no longer disappears after opening a file.
  • Numbered list markers are no longer cut off in long notebooks.
  • Pasting or opening certain tables no longer crashes the notebook editor.
  • Quickly clicking tags in the tag tree no longer accidentally enters multi-select. Hold Cmd or Ctrl, and Shift for ranges, when you do want bulk selection.
  • Nested images in saved articles are no longer dropped when Recall merges the reader content.
  • Chat code blocks fall back to plain text when syntax highlighting fails, instead of going blank.
item.title: Recall release notes, August 19, 2026: Safari and Edge support, chat that suggests what to ask, images as cards and add 10 URLs at a time.

item.author: Sankari Nair
item.description:
Excited to share that we have improved our Search flow in Recall!

Search has moved out of the small popup and into your library, so results now fill the full page. That means a lot more room to see what you've found, and everything you'd normally do with your cards still works on the results.

FYI: The improvement lands on desktop first, with a mobile overhaul to follow shortly.

What’s New

  • Search inside your content, not just titles. Recall now looks through your reader content, notes and quizzes, not just card titles. Each result shows a small counter for where the matches are (reader, notebook, quiz). You can hover over it to preview the matching text and click to jump straight to it.
  • Text search or AI search. Switch between the two right in the search bar. Text search finds exact words and phrases, best for names, keywords and specific terminology. AI search understands meaning rather than keywords, best for fuzzy or multi-lingual queries when you can't remember the exact wording.
  • Results are real cards. Because results appear in your library, you can stay in grid, list or table view, select multiple results (including shift-select), and run bulk actions like tagging or deleting on exactly what you searched for.
  • Combine search with filters. Narrow results further by tag, source, date or shared status. Filter options now only show what's actually in your current results, along with matching counts, so you're never offered a tag or source that returns nothing.
  • Related tags. When your search matches tag names, they appear above the results. Click one to turn your search into a tag filter.
  • Search from anywhere. Press “Cmd + /” on Mac, or “Ctrl + /” on Windows from any screen, including while reading a card, and you'll land in your library with the search bar focused and ready.
  • Search history. Recent searches appear when you focus the search bar, and restoring one brings back your search mode as well as the query.
  • Better empty state. When nothing matches, Recall tells you what you searched for and offers one-click ways out, such as clear the search and filters, or retry the same query with AI search.

Improvements

  • Better failure messaging on PDF uploads. Invalid, corrupted, password-protected and oversized PDFs now fail with a clear message instead of a generic one.
  • Longer AI persona instructions. You can now write up to 10,000 characters of custom persona instructions.

Fixes

  • Sync is more resilient: expired sessions refresh automatically instead of interrupting syncing.
  • Better layout on iPad. Headers, drawers and controls no longer sit under the status bar or notch in desktop-style layouts on iPad Pro.
  • Copying code from chat. Code copied out of chat now keeps its line breaks and array indexes (like arr[0]) intact.
  • Scrollable language selector on extension settings. You can now scroll the improved list of summary and translation languages on the settings page.
item.title: Recall release notes - July 30, 2026 - Search your whole library, right where your cards are

item.author: Sankari Nair
item.description:
Hello everyone, this release focuses on making the things you already rely on more reliable!

We completely rebuilt social saves, added a table view for your home page and expanded AI languages (now supporting 62 languages) and more models on Max. There is also an incredible customer story to check out and an open AMA with a Recall power user on building a second brain running through the end of the week.

What's New

Stronger social saves

We released social support around two weeks ago, but ran into many hiccups where Instagram transcripts or articles were not fully saved. We completely rebuilt the way we capture, transcribe, and present social content, and we are excited to relaunch it. Instagram, TikTok, X, LinkedIn, Reddit, and Facebook posts now save more reliably, with the post embed and the extracted text together in the reader where it makes sense, including transcripts for video posts.

Table view for your library

On the Items page you can now switch to a table view to scan, sort, and manage your knowledge base more efficiently, including tags, sources (websites, notes, and PDFs), and connection counts.

More AI languages

AI language support is much broader - now supporting 62 languages! Choose the language you want for summaries, quizzes, and tags, including Traditional Chinese, with clearer separation from chat translation. Caption and transcript language matching is also more accurate for Simplified versus Traditional Chinese.

New AI models

More models are in the picker on the Max Plan, including GPT-5.6 Terra, GPT-5.6 Luna, and Grok 4.5, so you can pick the right model for the job. We'll be releasing more documentation on which model to use when, but here's a quick TLDR.

  • Auto: Best for most users, lets Recall choose the right model for the task.
  • Quick/simple tasks: Gemini 3.5 Flash
  • Writing: Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.6 Terra
  • Complex reasoning: Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.6 Terra, DeepSeek V4 Pro
  • Research: Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Sonnet 5, GPT-5.6 Terra
  • Technical work: Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Sonnet 5, DeepSeek V4 Pro, GPT-5.6 Terra
  • Fast responses: Gemini 3.5 Flash, GPT-5.6 Luna, Grok 4.5

Customer story - Ricardo Yule's nine-step trails

Ricardo Yule shares how he went from almost abandoning his second brain to chatting with it every day. He shares his story in a Nine Trail Field Guide to Recall, as well as an interview with our marketing manager Nicole. We are also running an Ask Me Anything about second-brain workflows, open now and running through the end of the week. Drop your questions any time.

  • Join the AMA on Reddit until the end of this week.
  • Don't miss his inspiring nine-step field guide to Recall.

Improvements and Bugs

Improved AI for tags, connections, summaries, and quizzes

  • Tags reuse your existing tree more often
  • Connections focus on the core topics in a card rather than incidental mentions
  • Summaries better separate concise vs detailed (with stronger accuracy checks, especially on YouTube); and
  • Quizzes are more reliable, better balanced, and calibrated for learning.

Reading and library

  • You can set Reader as your default tab again. Reorder your tabs so Reader comes first, and cards will open straight into the reading view.
  • Scrollbars stay out of the way until you scroll
  • Wikidata sources show a proper source icon on reference cards
  • Simpler persona selection in chat - the last used persona is now the default.

Saving and reliability

  • More resilient podcast transcript fetching when the transcript provider blips
  • Sharing a link into Recall that fails to save no longer leaves you on a broken screen
  • Deleting a note no longer removes images that are still used in other notes

Editor

  • Markdown tables paste with working column resize and multi-cell selection
  • Creating a connection from selected text returns focus to the editor
  • Fixed crashes when searching for connections, editing complex lists, and applying formatting across table cells

Coming Next

For the next few weeks we will have a continued focus on improving reliability and giving you a smoother experience before tackling some of our more exciting features.

Also on the way:

  • Improved search: By moving search results out of the modal and into the full-screen knowledge base, you will have more control and more actions available for each result.
  • Improved chat: This will continue to be an ongoing investment, starting from chat-suggested questions through to an omnipresent chat and ongoing UI and UX improvements, like the ability to save multiple chat outputs to a single notebook.
  • Safari extension: Yes, this is finally in the works.
  • Faster, more reliable mobile sharing: Ideally you can share content to Recall, not wait for it to load, and trust that it will be saved to your knowledge base. This will be the first step in the development of the write API.
item.title: Recall release notes - July 23, 2026 - Rebuilt social saves, table view, more AI languages and models

item.author: Sankari Nair
item.description:
Recall started as a simple place to save the things you cared about. It has grown into something much bigger. This release marks that shift with the launch of our Use Case Hub, alongside the groundwork for a smarter, more integrated search experience.

Recall Use Case Hub

We get asked all the time "what should I actually use Recall for?" and now there is a proper home for the answer. What had started as a great place to save your interests from health research and recipes has now evolved into a powerful research, writing, AI, and knowledge engine.

The use case hub (site & docs) is a growing library of guides showing how real people put Recall to work, from grounding deep research and writing in your own sources to building a movie recommendation tracker.

Filter the use case hub for a high level overview, which links out to our docs for step by step guides:

  • By workflow - what your primary use case for Recall is, from daily productivity to curating a knowledge base grounded in the experts you trust.
  • By persona - who you are, whether that is a researcher, student, marketer, hobbyist, or someone using Recall for enhanced focus.
  • By content type - what you are saving, from PDFs and articles to social content like Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, and YouTube Shorts.

This is a resource we will continue to invest in, so please share your personal use cases and how we can improve them. We want to know which guides are genuinely useful, which are missing, and where a deeper dive would help.

A Step Towards Improved Search

We also have a bigger vision for search. Rather than living inside a modal, we want your results to surface right in the main home page view, so exploring your knowledge base feels seamless instead of tucked away in a popup. This release is a step towards that, while we keep iterating on a smoother experience.

Filter your library from the items page by tags, date range, source (websites, notes, and PDFs), and shared status. Includes multi-select, untagged cards, counts per option, and filters that persist after refresh.

Improvements & Bug Fixes:

Multi-Select Cards from the Tag Tree: Shift-click to select a range of tags in the tag tree for bulk actions.

Larger PDF uploads: upload files up to 250 MB (previously 100 MB).

Growing chat input: the chat box now expands as you type longer messages, up to 12 lines.

Improved reliability: This has and will continue to be a core focus, ensuring that sharing content across devices continues to work smoothly.

  • Going offline while saving content no longer loses your work. Saving recovers automatically once you are back online.
  • Recall appears more reliably in the Android share sheet when sharing links or files from other apps.

Notebook improvements:

  • Improved notebook sync across devices.
  • More reliable pasting of images into notebooks.
  • Notebook connections typed with spaces in the name now work correctly on iOS.

Improved content support:

  • Journal articles from sites like Elsevier and JNS now keep inline citation markers, render tables correctly, and preserve content after the references section.
  • Improved Wikipedia support: sharing Wikipedia links from email or social apps no longer fails when the URL includes tracking parameters.

Other Bug Fixes

  • Knowledge graph now displays correctly when viewing a card in split view.
  • Using your browser's translate feature (for example Google Translate) no longer crashes the app when adding a link through the add content dialog.
  • Quiz questions show clearer feedback: multiple-choice explanations align correctly, and true/false answers now show the correct response when you get one wrong.

Coming Soon

For the next few weeks we will be focused on improving reliability and giving you a smoother experience before tackling some of our more exciting features.

While we launched a lot of new content support recently (such as LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and more), we have noticed that reliability has not been where we would like it. We have prioritized improving support for these platforms.

Also on the way:

  • Improved Chat: This will continue to be an ongoing investment, starting from chat-suggested questions through to an omnipresent chat and ongoing UI/UX improvements, like the ability to save multiple chat outputs to a single notebook.
  • Improved tagging and connections: upgrading our LLM models and the algorithms behind AI-generated tags and connections.
  • More language support. This has been on our list for a while, and you can expect many more languages soon.
  • Safari extension! Yes this is finally in the works.
  • Faster, more reliable mobile sharing. Ideally you can share content to Recall, not wait for it to load, and trust that it will be saved to your knowledge base. This will be the first step in the development of the write API.
item.title: Recall Release Notes: 12 July, 2026 - The Use Cases Hub, plus a Step Towards Improved Search

item.author: Sankari Nair
item.description:
Excited to share that there's been a big increase in the content we support, with a lot more still on its way.

New features

In the last month, we've added several new sources that Recall supports. You can find the full list of everything we support here. Everything you save is automatically summarized and organized for you, and the best part is you can chat across all of it.

Whether you're drafting an email, finding recipe inspiration, or just using Recall as your everyday chat, your sources come first and the internet second. Save more, and watch your own knowledge resurface when you need it.

  • Instagram support: Save Instagram posts and Reels from the app or browser extension.
  • LinkedIn support: Save LinkedIn posts and articles directly from the app or browser extension. Profile pages and non-post URLs are not supported.
  • Text and Markdown file uploads: Upload .txt and .md files from Add Content, including bulk upload on Plus. Plain text becomes paragraph blocks; Markdown is parsed into formatted notebook content. On mobile, you can also share text files or plain text directly into Recall from other apps.

Improvements & fixes

  • Large notebook performance: Drag-and-drop block reordering is limited on very large notes to keep the editor responsive.
  • Reader accuracy: Bracketed text in saved articles (e.g. [like this]) no longer renders incorrectly as math equations.
  • Images in tables: Images inside notebook table cells now stay within the cell, remain resizable, and scale correctly when columns are resized.
  • More reliable mobile navigation: Back-button behavior is more predictable across chat, settings, text-to-speech, item creation, and Add Content flows.
  • Shared note cards: Saving a shared card that contains only notebook content (no web page) now indexes it for chat and search immediately, without needing to edit the notebook first.
  • Chat-created cards: Cards created by the chat agent stay openable even when the source URL cannot be scraped; your notebook content is preserved.
item.title: Recall release notes, 26 June 2026: Instagram, LinkedIn, and more

item.author: Sankari Nair
item.description:
You know the frustration of giving your AI the same instructions over and over. No em dashes, no unnecessary colons, more professional please. Well, those days are over!

A persona is simply a set of instructions you give Recall once that tells it how to respond. Think of it as a consistent role, a consistent tone, and a consistent set of rules it follows before it generates anything. You set it once, and it just works from then on. Open the Recall Global Chat and click on the icon in the top left-hand corner to create your first persona.

Learn more: Read the Personas docs.

Why it's useful

  • Consistency. Your brand voice, tone, and rules stay the same across every chat, with no drift.
  • Speed. Set your instructions once instead of copy-pasting them into every conversation.
  • Specialization. Tailor a persona to a specific job. A research persona goes deep and cites its sources. A writing persona drops the citations so the copy stays clean and on-brand.

What you can do

  • Create a persona with a role, a goal, the behaviors and rules you want, and a tone and style.
  • Set custom rules that Recall follows every time, such as pulling exact timestamps from YouTube videos, citing every source for research, or avoiding buzzwords and hashtags when writing.
  • Set a default persona that persists across the browser extension, the mobile app, and single-card chats. Toggle it on or off whenever you like.
  • Switch personas per task, or stay on the standard prompt-free Recall persona as your baseline.

How to create your first persona

  1. Open chat and go to the Personas menu in the left-hand corner.
  2. Click Add new persona and give it a name.
  3. Enter your instructions covering role, goal, behavior, tone, and rules.
  4. Save the persona, then select it in any chat. Set it as your default if you like.

We have been having a lot of fun testing this over the last few days. Personas are new and we are still iterating, so please try building one for research and one for writing, then let us know how they fit into your workflow and how we can improve them.
item.title: Recall release notes, 18 June 2026: Introducing Custom Personas

item.author: Sankari Nair
item.description:
Hello everyone, a few simple yet impactful updates to Recall, with more to come soon.

New

  • Group your home page by time: Organize your cards by when you added or updated them, so it's easier to pick up where you left off.
  • Save from Apple News: You can now save and read Apple News articles in Recall.
  • Passwordless sign-in with a verification code: You can now log in using a one-time code sent to you, instead of relying only on a password. This makes signing in faster and means you don't have to remember or reset a password to get back into your account.

Improvements

  • Tag input focuses automatically: The tag box now focuses as soon as you open it, stays open so you can add several tags in a row, and works smoothly on mobile and the browser extension.
  • Full-size images from Wix sites: Images saved from Wix-based websites now load in full resolution instead of small thumbnails.
  • Faster spaced repetition reviews: Review sessions now load and respond more quickly, which is especially noticeable if you have a large library of saved items to work through.
  • Easier access to chat: We've made it quicker to get into chat from the desktop header and given it a more prominent spot, so asking the AI a question takes fewer clicks to reach.

Fixes

  • Fixed long tags spilling outside their container and overlapping other text on small mobile devices.
  • Fixed Wikipedia articles with special characters in their title (like "%") failing to open on iPhone and iPad.
  • Fixed tables sometimes disappearing from notes when you export, copy, or share them.
  • Fixed LaTeX equations so math and formulas render properly in both chat and notebooks, rather than appearing as raw code.
  • Fixed regenerating an AI chat summary so it no longer fails or gets stuck.
  • Fixed adding connections within collapsible (toggle) headings in the editor, which previously wasn't possible.

From the community

We sat down with AI consultant Paul Phelps, who uses Recall as his second brain. He walked us through how he captures research, client notes, and long-form reading in one place, and how he relies on chat and spaced repetition to actually retain and resurface what he saves.

Want to share how you use Recall? We'd love to feature you. to tell us about your use case.
item.title: Recall release notes, 15 June 2026: Group cards on your home page by date, Apple News support, and more

item.author: Sankari Nair
item.description:
This update is packed with improvements across Recall, the big one being multi-select, so you can now export and chat with several cards at once. Worth reading the notes in full. There are a good number of fixes in here that should make everything run smoother.

New

  • Multi Select and Export to Markdown. Select multiple cards in your knowledge base and download them all as Markdown files in a single ZIP, so you can back up your notes or move them into another app.
  • Multi Select and Chat with multiple cards. Select several cards at once and start a chat that uses all of them as context, making it easier to ask questions across related notes.

Tip: hold Shift, click your first card, then click the last card in the range to select everything in between.

Enablement

We've been putting Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 through their paces for research and writing inside Recall. All the details of the three-prompt test for research writing and recommendations in our blog.

Improved

  • Combined display menu. Sorting and view options now live in one place, so you can switch between grid and list, change the sort field, and flip the order without hunting through separate controls.
  • Better Substack & Wordpress saving. Articles from Substack and Wordpress now save with more complete content and headings, so less of the original page is lost.
  • More reliable Arc imports. Saving and importing content in the Arc browser now uses a more dependable method for fetching page content.
  • Smarter duplicate detection. The extension and app now recognize when two URLs point to the same page, so you're less likely to end up with duplicate saves of the same content.
  • Easier mobile editing. On phones, it's now easier to add a new line when your cursor sits just above the floating formatting toolbar.

Fixed

  • Search now closes correctly. Pressing Escape and clicking the close button now reliably dismiss the search window, which previously could stay open.
  • Tag actions on mobile. The tag actions menu no longer gets stuck after navigating back on mobile.
  • Editor crash on broken tables. Notes containing malformed tables no longer crash the editor when you open them.
  • Math and LaTeX display. Mathematical formulas now render correctly in chat and in your notes.
  • List formatting in notes. Numbered and bulleted lists no longer get cut off or misaligned when you increase the reader text size.
  • Regenerating toggle sections. Regenerating content inside a toggle block now shows a loading indicator and keeps your existing content if something goes wrong.
  • Connections in toggle headings. You can now add connections to other cards from within toggle headings.

We are starting to scope what's next. Stay tuned, and thank you for all the input in helping us shape the upcoming roadmap.
